analysis.title: Kennametal Inc. (KMT): F1Q27 First Take: Tungsten driven beat, core business inline
key_insights: KMT reported F1Q27 segment EBIT $87mn above Visible Alpha (VA) consensus. GS estimates all of the beat came from better tungsten price/cost (~$95mn) versus expectations, so the core business was inline.
F1Q27 EPS was $3.48 reported versus GS/VA consensus of $2.65/$2.65. GS estimates EPS would have been ~$0.39 excluding the $3.09 tungsten price/cost benefit.
Free operating cash flow (FOCF) fell to -$212mn because of a large tungsten-driven inventory investment.
KMT raised its FY27 adjusted EPS guide to $5.00-$6.00 from $4.15-$5.15 (GS/consensus: $5.20/$5.00). The raise reflects the 1Q27 EPS beat, and the organic growth outlook of ~+41% to +47% is unchanged.
KMT left its FY27 sales guide unchanged at $3,330mn-$3,450mn (VA consensus $3,383mn). The guide assumes price/volume of 41.5%/2.5%.
KMT introduced an F2Q27 EPS guide of $1.20-$1.50 versus consensus of $1.34.
F1Q27 organic growth was +54% (GS +53.8%). Infrastructure grew +97% (GS +90%) and Metal Cutting grew +29% (GS +32%).
GS views the result as fairly inline and expects the stock to trade accordingly. GS rates KMT Sell with a $33 12-month price target versus a $30.53 price, 8.1% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell rating and $33 target, based on 8.5x Q5-Q8E EBITDA. It sees the tungsten-driven beat as a fairly inline result with the core business inline.

earnings_insights: KMT F1Q27 reported EPS $3.48 (reported 11/4/26) vs GS est $2.65 and VA consensus $2.65. Excluding the $3.09 tungsten price/cost benefit, GS estimates EPS would have been ~$0.39.

KMT F1Q27 segment operating income $380mn (reported) vs GS est $283mn and VA consensus $293mn. Infrastructure segment EBIT was $262mn vs GS est $180mn and VA $185mn. Metal Cutting segment EBIT was $118mn vs GS est $103mn and VA $107mn.

KMT F1Q27 revenue $775mn (reported) vs GS est $768mn... correction: reported $768mn vs GS est/VA consensus $775mn, a 0.9% miss against GS. Infrastructure revenue was $370mn vs GS $360mn, and Metal Cutting revenue was $398mn vs GS $415mn.

KMT raised its FY27 adjusted EPS guide to $5.00-$6.00 from $4.15-$5.15 (GS est $5.20, consensus $5.00). The guide assumes organic growth of ~+41% to +47% and keeps the FY27 sales guide at $3,330mn-$3,450mn (VA consensus $3,383mn).
KMT introduced an F2Q27 EPS guide of $1.20-$1.50 vs consensus of $1.34.

GS FY27E (June 2026 fiscal year-end) estimates: revenue $3,349mn, EBITDA $713mn, EPS $5.20. FY28E: revenue $3,490mn, EBITDA $379mn, EPS $2.00. Quarterly GS EPS estimates are 12/26E $1.50 and 3/27E $0.45.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell view: General Engineering organic growth better than expected, stronger operating leverage, and better FCF conversion.
FY28E EPS of $2.00 is well below FY27E $5.20 in GS estimates, which reflects the tungsten price/cost benefit not recurring.
Inventory investment tied to tungsten pushed F1Q27 FOCF to -$212mn.
